title: On the Record: A Press Briefing at WKU

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: Good morning. I've called this briefing to address the questions that have been circulating about the new English language requirement.

dialogue.speaker: Reporter 1
dialogue.text: Rector, can you confirm whether all students will be required to pass a B2 English assessment to graduate?

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: The university has decided that from the 2027 intake, students will need to demonstrate B2 English proficiency. However, this applies to new students only. Current students are not affected.

dialogue.speaker: Reporter 2
dialogue.text: Some faculty members have suggested this would put additional pressure on students from non-urban areas. How do you respond?

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: We acknowledge that access to English-language preparation varies across regions. That's why we're announcing today that the university will fund English preparation courses for all first-year students from next autumn.

dialogue.speaker: Reporter 1
dialogue.text: Did you consult students before making this decision?

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: The student council was informed of the proposal in February and was invited to provide feedback. Their feedback was considered during the final decision-making process.

dialogue.speaker: Reporter 2
dialogue.text: The student council president has claimed that they were not given sufficient time to respond properly. Do you dispute that?

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: I wouldn't say "dispute." I'd say that the timeline was challenging, and I accept that the consultation process could have been longer. We intend to improve this for future policy decisions.

dialogue.speaker: Reporter 1
dialogue.text: Will students who fail the B2 assessment be denied graduation?

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: Students who do not meet the requirement will be offered additional support and multiple assessment opportunities. We have no intention of withholding graduation from students who make genuine effort.

dialogue.speaker: Reporter 2
dialogue.text: Finally, what would you say to students who are worried about this change?

dialogue.speaker: Rector
dialogue.text: I'd tell them that this requirement reflects the reality of the professional world they are entering. English proficiency is not an add-on — it is a core professional skill. And I would assure them that the university will support them in achieving it.
